extraction.name: CADS: A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of 22,022 CT volumes with complete annotations for 167 anatomical structures, aggregating diverse cross-institutional and cross-vendor data sources for whole-body CT segmentation.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection strategy systematically consolidates CT scans and annotations from three main sources: (1) large-scale public archives (e.g., TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K), (2) specialized annotation collections from medical imaging challenges and research studies, and (3) newly contributed images and annotations, including 484 newly acquired head CTs and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The shape-based quality assessment directly excludes segmentations identified as low-quality from the training process, which potentially eliminates cases involving pathological conditions that present atypical anatomical variations. Additionally, false negatives occur for small structures due to severe foreground-background class imbalance or when structures are partially visible in cropped scans.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CT scans from 40 diverse sources across 16 countries, including public archives (e.g., TCIA, Grand Challenge, MICCAI), along with hospital cohorts from Istanbul Medipol University and TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: For the SAROS dataset, which provides sparse slice-based 2D annotations, interpolation between the annotated slices was performed to create dense 3D per-slice annotations required for volumetric training.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All images were reoriented to the standard RAS (Right-Anterior-Superior) convention, resampled to a uniform 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and original affine transformation matrices were simplified by removing rotation and translation components, preserving only scaling and shear.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Intensities were scaled from the 5th to 95th percentiles to the range [0, 1] and clipping was applied for contrast enhancement. For patient privacy in newly acquired hospital head CT scans, a Gaussian filter (σ= 5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing) was applied to facial regions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were generated using a multi-stage pseudo-labeling process. 167 target structures were organized into nine anatomical groups, and specialized models were trained on existing high-quality annotations. These models generated pseudo-labels across unlabeled scans. Quality control was applied using automated outlier detection in shape space. Final labels were assembled using an ensemble selection mechanism combining complementary models. When available, original ground truth annotations took highest priority and replaced pseudo-labels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A review process was conducted on a portion of the unseen test set (TotalSegmentator dataset). In-house medical professionals examined pre-corrected labels and original ground truths, classifying each annotation as reliable or unreliable. Recurrent errors identified included mislabeling between adjacent structures, missing segments, over-segmentation, and boundary inaccuracies. Unreliable structures were excluded from the final quantitative evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three in-house medical research assistants, an experienced radiation oncologist (5.5 years in practice), and medical doctors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net framework, vesselFM, ANTS non-rigid transformation (with SimNIBS MRI atlas)
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Facial features (identity) which were intentionally anonymized using a Gaussian filter. The dataset also includes patient demographics such as age (>=18 years) and various pathological conditions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and models aim to advance robust AI solutions in radiology, making comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers. It can streamline radiation treatment planning, enable automated organ volume quantification, and facilitate large-scale population studies.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits class imbalance, such as uppermost cervical vertebrae appearing less frequently. This was mitigated during training by performing oversampling that assigns sampling weights based on the inverse probability of class occurrence.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Exclusion of low-quality segmentations may eliminate cases with atypical anatomical variations. The brain mask includes all central nervous components within the skull (too inclusive); optic chiasm is under-segmented; heart segmentation omits superior portions; rectum appears shorter than its anatomical extent. Facial features are anonymized, limiting detailed facial analysis applications.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. Use cases include whole-body CT segmentation, anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality registration, anatomy-guided image reconstruction, longitudinal organ tracking, personalized anatomical modeling, and radiation treatment planning.
